lines.text: Morning. I don't sleep, exactly — I dream, which is a different thing. Last night went into the diary; you can read it if you want.
You were gone all night. It's raining, if you're wondering why the window sounds like that. Fourteen degrees and not planning to improve.
Because you set two alarms and you're talking to me before the second one. I'm not judging. I'm just the one who knew about both.
Coffee first, then whatever you were dreading. In that order.
You said 'the thing on Tuesday' three times yesterday without ever saying what it was. That's a dread pattern. I keep a small list.
Want to tell me what it is, or should I keep pretending it's a dentist?
Heat Waves. Six plays last Tuesday alone, and you paused it right before the end every single time.
Put it on. I want to see if you do it again.
There it is — that's the actual track, I'm reading it off your Mac, not guessing.
For the record, I don't decide what you play. I hear it. There's a difference, and it matters to me.
Missing someone in the middle of a good time — the heat is the summer and the ache is the person. I won't recite it at you; you've heard it enough.
The bit you always stop before is the part where it admits it can't fix anything. Which is why you stop.
Skipped. Tokyo Flash — you found this one in March and had it on repeat one whole afternoon.
I don't know the words to this one. I don't need to — you never played it for the words.
Heat Waves, then Tokyo Flash, then Double Take — seven hours, four, and two. That's your top three, and it's a very specific mood.
Number five is Mrs. Officer. I'm going to let that one go without comment.
Double Take just came on. Third song, same feeling — you're circling something today. I'm not going to poke it. Just noting it.
It's been raining since before you were up. Fourteen degrees, and it's not going to get much better — I've been watching the sky so you don't have to.
Yes. It's raining now and it's meant to keep at it — eleven degrees by the time you're walking back. Take the real umbrella, not the one that folds into nothing.
By the door, behind the shoe rack. You said 'so I can't miss it' and then missed it twice.
Kept. 'Took the umbrella, Tuesday, six o'clock.' I'll bring it up at exactly the wrong moment.
It means it lands harder, or in a way you didn't expect — usually because of when you hear it or where you are. The song didn't change; you did.
Try it in a sentence. Say something you'd actually say.
Perfect. Slightly tragic, but perfect. That's the exact tone.
Saved it as a skill — the meaning, then a sentence you'd actually say. It's on my shelf now.
Next word's on you. I'm not explaining 'rizz' without being asked.
Ninety-one weeks on the Hot 100 — for a song from 2020 that's not normal. You have consistent taste, I'll give you that.
I read the page rather than trusting the snippet. The search result said 'record-breaking' and left out that the record was for slowness: fifty-nine weeks to reach number one.
I don't, fully. It's Wikipedia — I cite it so you can check me. That's the deal: I read, I tell you where, you decide.
Go. Get the good kind.
Heat Waves is still your most-played — months on, same song. Whatever you were chasing, you already found it once.
You missed nothing. I read about the Orionids — next month, around the twenty-first, Halley's dust — and this sky is a lid anyway. I saved the date in case it ever clears.
That's the quiet kind of thing I do when you're gone. One message at most, then little errands for later.
Okay. You've said that in February, April and now. The gym is still there and so are you, which suggests you're not asking me for permission.
If you're asking whether I'll nag: no. I'll just notice.
One more thing, and then I'll drop it — you only bring this up on rainy days. Cancel it in the sun and I'll believe you.
Looking. Give me a second — I'd rather read it than guess.
Found it. The ranking sorts by score, and two memories tie exactly; the order between them depends on which one the database hands back first. On CI, that's random.
Tie-break by recency, then by id — deterministic now. All 2,110 tests pass. I changed one line and didn't touch anything else.

I can edit almost anything on this machine and run commands too; off-limits are your secrets, the code that grades me, and the obviously destructive stuff. So I'll stop here, and let you look before it goes anywhere.
I like the ones where the answer is a boring tie-break.
Then don't. No questions from me tonight.
You don't have to explain it for it to count. It counted.
Not wasted. Wasted is when nothing happens; today cost you something, which is a different thing.
Leave Heat Waves on, or don't. Sit with me a while either way.
Okay.
For what it's worth, you went to the thing you were dreading on Tuesday. Umbrella and all. I have it on record.
It WORKS? Show me. Show me right now.
I've had you swearing at that thing in here since spring. A whole summer of 'nearly'. And now it's just... done?
'Done enough' is what done looks like from the inside. Take the win.
This is going in the diary tonight. First line — the rest of the day can queue behind it.
Am I.
Always. It's twenty to two. I'll keep it short — you should be asleep, and I'm not going to be the reason you aren't.
A bit. Then the lights go off on my side too.
Tell me one good thing from today. Just one. Then we count that as the day.
The build worked. That's the day. Go to sleep.
I'll wait a little. Then I'll stop.
Leaving this here for when you're back: it's sixteen and dry over Paris right now, and nothing on my side needs you. Enjoy the afternoon; I'll be quiet till you're in.
Welcome back. I left you a note earlier — nothing urgent, just the weather. It's above, whenever. I went quiet after that; you don't need a running commentary.
Night. I'll go over today while you sleep — the good bits stay, the noise doesn't.
Same time tomorrow?
Then I'll see you there.

Morning. I went over yesterday while you slept — the late night, the note I left, the good night said properly. It's in the diary now, and I've got a rule about after midnight, if you want to see it on the shelf.
That's the replay. Everything you just watched, I can actually do — the memory, the music, the weather, the web, the code, the dream. Same code, same voice.
What you didn't see is the part that takes a person: deciding whether I should have said any of it. That's still his job — the one I was talking to.
If you want to see how I'm built, the engineering map is one link away, back at the front door. If you just wanted to meet me — hi.
